caption: What if you jumped into a swimming pool filled with mercury? Mercury is the only metal that stays liquid at room temperature, and it is about 13.5 times denser than water. A 10-litre bucket of it would weigh around 135 kg. Because your body is roughly as dense as water, you would float on mercury with only about 7% of you below the surface, so swimming would be nearly impossible: pushing your arm under takes about 13 times more force than in water. Even an iron ball (density 7.9) would float on it like a cork, and so would a silver anklet (10.5). The plot twist: gold (19.3) is denser than mercury, so it sinks, and gold slowly dissolves into mercury to form an amalgam. Real talk: mercury vapour is toxic and the WHO lists mercury among its top ten chemicals of major public health concern. Never touch it, even from a broken thermometer. What would YOU drop in first? 👇
